title: Duke's snubs of Sonny Greer and Ray Nance on the concert night
summary: Duke brushed off Sonny Greer, introduced Bigard briefly and played the tune too slowly, and never called Ray Nance from the wings.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So when the curtain went up for the concert, Sonny was downstairs. They called me down. I came down and I sat. And Duke was announcing. So all of a sudden he called, "Here's the great Greer." And that's all. The boy hadn't gotten off the drums yet. Sonny had to climb up on that stage to get on the drums and Duke said, "We're going to do a little something we did together for a while." And Sonny was trying to ask him, "What are you going to play? What are you going to do?" He said, "That's all right. Just follow." So Duke started playing anything and Sonny was just fooling with the drums and hitting the cymbals. And first thing, you know, Duke said, "Oh, that's enough of that," and then went back to the mike, left Sonny up there. Sonny had to hop down off that stage to get back out. And that's all he said about Sonny.

I said, "What is this business?" So I sat there and he turned around to look, to see, and he saw me there and he saw me looking at him, and all he says then, "And now I'd like to introduce one of my fine clarinetists I had in the band, Barney

Bigard." Boom, that was it.
He got up there so I started -- he gave an introduction, playing the tune, and he's playing it slow, like a drag. And now it's getting to be sixteen -- and I said, "No, keep your cool. Just go ahead and bear with it." And I'm trying to get him to pick it up, pick up -- but he can't get to him. He don't want to see that at all. Okay, so I go through and the thing was -- the people, whatever it was, they liked it anyway, and I could have taken an encore or anything. That was it. So I said, "Well, that's fine."

So now Nance is in the wings all dressed up and his fiddle's raring to go. He never did call Nance. Never. I said, "Well, I'll be darned." And he had some old funny singers -- I don't know whether they were European singers or what. Girls, a couple of girls or something like that. Did you know that?
I know there was one girl he brought from, I think, Scandinavia and another one from Canada.
Yeah, there was that -- it didn't mean a thing, absolutely nothing.
One was very good and one was terrible.
So, I mean, and that's what happened.
And I said, "What is with this man?"
